key_insight: Component-level cost models project global solar LCOE near 8 USD/MWh by 2050, while onshore wind reaches about 43 USD/MWh as non-declining balance-of-system costs limit further reductions.
engineering_relevance: Solar and wind planning should account for distinct component-cost trends and persistent national differences rather than relying solely on global averages.
method: Curate a comprehensive database of national solar and wind costs.
Decompose national LCOE into components and model their trends separately.
Model national deviations from global costs and compare projections with integrated assessment models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports roughly 12% annual declines in both solar module and balance-of-system costs since 1990, versus 4% for wind turbines and no decline in wind balance-of-system costs.
watch_item: The 2050 values are model projections, not guarantees; the abstract does not quantify forecast uncertainty or detailed validation performance.
paper_title: Will national renewable costs continue declining?
